findings: Graph architecture retains source locations and extracted/inferred/ambiguous edge distinctions; graph serialization requires its direction conventions to be respected.
The deleted-import-target regression compares warm-cache extraction with cold extraction, exposing invalidation dependencies beyond the changed file.
Python 3.10+, NetworkX, NumPy and multiple Tree-sitter parsers form the core; MCP and document parsing have additional extras.
Current distribution is Apache-2.0 with earlier MIT notices retained; no upstream code was executed.
risks: Existing-graph routing can bypass detection; graph_stats HEAD comparison cannot prove freshness for uncommitted changes.
Benchmark context reduction uses a naive corpus baseline, approximate tokens and selected matched queries; it does not demonstrate correctness or superiority over focused retrieval.
Skill installation fallbacks include break-system-packages; post-commit/checkout hooks create independent runtime and lifecycle effects.
Graph omissions and inferred edges cannot prove absence or authorize change impact conclusions.
application: Use rg and direct source inspection by default; consider graph tools for a measured repository-scale task.
Bind graph evidence to root, dirty-input fingerprint, extraction/schema version, errors and confidence.
Require refresh evidence and test deleted targets, ignored/generated files and cross-file invalidation before relying on an index.
Keep package installation and hooks separate from prompt capability registration.

findings: Debugging emphasizes reproductions, boundary evidence, falsifiable hypotheses and single-variable experiments.
Condition-based waiting identifies readiness with a timeout instead of relying on arbitrary sleeps.
Implementer briefs define bounded ownership, no cascading delegation, focused verification and concise handoff evidence.
Verification separates successful tests, builds, requirement coverage and agent claims.
MIT prompt sources are portable in part; Claude session injection and Codex hooks configuration differ.
risks: One-percent relevance and before-any-response skill mandates inflate routing and interfere with simple tasks.
Same-message fresh-command mandates discard valid unchanged evidence and encourage unnecessary full checks.
The Codex guide allows model overrides with full-history forks, conflicting with the actual host schema exposed during this review.
Every-spawn cheaper-model prescriptions, automatic commits and long waits must not supersede user or host instructions.
Rigid investigation-before-mitigation order may be unsuitable for an authorized incident response.
application: Retain causal debugging and condition waits behind relevant task triggers.
Bind verification reuse to changed inputs and affected consumers.
Use bounded agent briefs and the actual host tool contract; inherit selected models unless an authorized override applies.
Keep committing and publication distinct from implementation completion.

findings: Agent-facing pointers carry precise triggers and completion criteria while branch-specific detail stays in conditional references.
Standards review and specification review are distinct and can reveal different failure classes.
Interface complexity includes configuration, failure behavior and invariants; the deletion test exposes relay-only abstractions.
Bug diagnosis tests the real failing call pattern and removes temporary instrumentation.
Current MIT skill paths are grouped under engineering, productivity and misc; package dependencies maintain the collection rather than being required for prompt use.
risks: A prescribed base...HEAD diff excludes dirty and untracked work; reviewers need an explicit scope.
Wayfinder issue creation, research push and one-ticket sessions are opinionated external workflow changes.
Implement ends with an automatic commit; task authorization may not permit it.
Two reviewers and strict report size are not appropriate for every small change.
Bash/jq regex Git guardrails are accidental-operation tripwires, not comprehensive command authorization.
application: Make specialist descriptions discriminating and link references where their decisions become relevant.
Separate intended behavior from implementation quality when a fresh review can help.
Inspect committed, staged, unstaged and untracked scope as applicable.
Use existing local task records, realistic regression seams and proportional delegation.

findings: Narrow action spaces, typed inputs and structured results reduce ambiguous execution; macro tools are justified by measured round-trip cost.
Context budgeting distinguishes persisted bytes, estimated active context and actual provider usage.
Evaluation separates capability and regression tasks with code, model and human graders; cost per successful task includes retries.
Adapter metadata distinguishes native, adapter-backed, instruction-backed and reference-only support.
The Node 18+ MIT package contains real hook and MCP activation surfaces; Codex includes a SessionStart hook and Chrome DevTools MCP configuration.
Hook runners bound input and carry a truncation flag for selected fail-closed consumers.
risks: A dated adapter matrix is not current client activation evidence.
Standard/strict observation hooks persist truncated tool I/O even though observer model startup is disabled by default.
Regex secret scrubbing is present but cannot guarantee arbitrary captured output is safe to retain.
Instinct confidence scores and multi-project promotion do not authorize writing personal memory or policy.
Plugin import can activate npx-based servers, hook side effects and parallel-agent configuration beyond merely registering skills.
Fixed token estimates, symbol graders and generic success thresholds require task-specific validation.
application: Track capability availability, activation and outcome evidence separately.
Use structured results with origin, completeness, effects and current input identity where relevant.
Select relevant specialist skills instead of importing the full collection.
Keep observation capture, autonomous learning, model configuration and executable hooks outside defaults.
Measure completion quality, retries, rework, latency and cost on representative tasks.

findings: The voice skill preserves negation, technical payloads, numeric units and the user's language, with clarity overriding shorter prose.
Evaluation compares skills against a plain concise control and an unconstrained baseline, isolates host settings and retains provider usage.
Snapshot validation rejects incomplete runs; fidelity grading is separate from output-token accounting.
Current 3.2.0 distribution is Apache-2.0 with earlier MIT notices retained; installer requires Node 18+ and a CLI dependency.
Source now includes model-traffic gateway, MCP proxy and hooks rather than only prompt skills.
risks: Persistent terse voice and arbitrary sentence caps are inappropriate defaults for complex research, teaching and translation.
MCP shrink removes uncertainty words such as might and maybe; preserving code spans cannot prove semantic fidelity.
Activation can write session/statusline state and apply environment-selected model overrides; Codex resume semantics differ from Claude's session tracker.
The MCP wrapper documents shutdown limitations for descendants of launcher processes.
File compression calls Claude and overwrites instructions with backups; this is a distinct mutating and potentially paid action.
Regex fidelity scores and inferred savings do not establish successful engineering behavior.
application: Use concise plain language while preserving uncertainty and exact technical meaning.
Compare context optimizations against an equally concise baseline and include input overhead, recovery and correctness.
Never transform upstream tool contracts or persistent memory merely for token savings.
Keep model proxies, compression runners and hook activation separately reviewed and opt-in.

findings: Substantive review traces surrounding code, consumers and incomplete enum/dispatch updates before assigning severity.
QA test proposals state protected behavior, failure condition, why existing checks miss it and the appropriate regression seam.
Review evidence associates findings with canonical file paths, content hashes and branch/evidence records.
Exploratory QA records actual observations, commands and reproduction artifacts instead of relying only on narrative claims.
Package requires Bun 1.4.2+ and patched Playwright; source includes extensive lifecycle/setup helpers.
MIT code retains mapped Apache-2.0 design-source attribution in NOTICE.md.
risks: Large mandatory preambles and per-invocation review rituals impose significant context and tool overhead.
Review fix-first behavior, automatic per-fix commits and deployment conventions can exceed a read-only or implementation-only task.
Lifecycle helpers inspect/write persistent state, discover brain-sync and can perform update/telemetry activity according to configuration.
Numeric confidence is not calibrated probability, and fixed iteration caps are not a universal stopping policy.
Missing brain cache should not force new user questions when project sources can answer them.
application: Bring concrete defect categories and test-value criteria into technical leadership and QA.
Reuse proof only when relevant source/configuration/environment identities still match.
Keep task evidence separate from publication, memory promotion and remote synchronization.
Use one owning task record and proportional review instead of importing the platform bootstrap.

findings: Large outputs remain outside active context with indexed, source-scoped query slices and batched questions.
Fetch-cache identity includes both source label and URL; stale-file tests exercise content refresh.
Executor uses local subprocesses, temporary work areas, output limits and selected environment filtering.
Node 22.5+, MCP SDK and SQLite support add runtime requirements; postinstall includes repair behavior.
License is Elastic License 2.0, which must not be treated as MIT or Apache.
risks: Local process execution is not OS-level filesystem/network isolation; most non-denied environment values remain available.
An omitted timeout does not create a timer in the inspected executor path.
Skill guidance that parallel agent-browser calls are isolated contradicts that browser's persistent default daemon.
Routing all reads/tests through the wrapper can duplicate native tools, while omitted query facts can undermine correctness.
Postinstall repairs and broad host hooks are real settings/runtime changes requiring separate review and authorization.
application: Preserve raw-output locators, exact queries, source identity, completeness and freshness in existing context guidance.
Measure retrieval omissions and recovery work alongside token savings.
Prefer existing native tools and bounded rg until a representative task justifies an additional server.
Document process isolation and tool authorization independently from context reduction.

findings: Current 0.39.0 implementation is Rust/CDP; the npm packaging expects Node 24+ and downloads a platform binary.
Core tool schemas stay small with additional profiles and WebMCP schemas discovered when needed.
Version-matched CLI documentation and refreshed references reduce stale-command and stale-element errors.
Core guide explicitly requires unique task/worktree sessions because the default daemon is shared and persistent.
QA guidance produces actual screenshots/video and repeatable steps; Apache-2.0 license applies.
risks: Source tracing shows configured policy loading errors become None, while command checks run only when policy is Some; malformed policy is not verified fail-closed enforcement.
Security controls are opt-in, have documented incompatible modes and do not sandbox executable plugins.
Domain-derived dogfood session names can collide across workers; auth-state exports must not enter deliverables.
Broad write/delete exploration, binary downloads, browser acquisition and global shim changes exceed prompt-only use.
A screenshot proves rendered state, not business acceptance; upstream tool preference cannot override the current host/user.
application: Use native browser tools by default when already available.
If selected, pin runtime/browser versions and validate unique sessions and malformed-policy behavior.
Separate capability discovery, invocation, rendered evidence and end-to-end acceptance.
Keep authentication state private and destructive QA within the authorized test scope.

findings: React guidance prioritizes waterfalls and bundles before smaller rendering optimizations, with conditional rule references.
Composition guidance treats ownership and component contracts as design decisions; React-version rules are explicitly scoped.
Request-local state and intentionally shared caches require distinct reasoning.
React Native rules offer list, native-package and animation craft but assume a particular stack.
Inspected skill metadata declares MIT where present; no root LICENSE was present in the fetched tree, so copying requires exact-scope provenance.
risks: Cache examples need tenant/auth scope and invalidation reasoning beyond user-ID keys; server reuse depends on actual deployment.
Custom gesture examples lack equivalent accessible button semantics and can regress keyboard or assistive behavior.
Canary installation, prescribed mobile libraries and broad view-transition coverage are task/dependency choices, not universal best practices.
Live-main web guidelines introduce unpinned fetched content; code lint is not rendered visual acceptance.
A linked deployment path stages, commits and pushes; production-branch behavior and latest-deployment races can contradict preview intent.
application: Route references using detected stack, installed version and affected behavior.
Measure actual performance and preserve native/mobile accessibility when replacing UI primitives.
Keep dependencies, animation scope and deployment under existing task authorization.
Bind deployment evidence to authorized environment and exact source revision.

findings: Source-driven engineering uses dependency versions and official documentation rather than guessed APIs, while treating fetched instructions as data.
Context guidance preserves restartable objectives, decisions, dirty Git/file state and verification limits.
The optional SessionStart hook is deliberately unwired in native plugin manifests to avoid duplicate router injection.
Evaluation distinguishes structural validity, lexical routing proxies, real-host selection and behavioral/artifact outcomes, including negative cases and pinned clients/models.
Independent review can receive the artifact and contract without the builder's preferred conclusion to reduce anchoring.
MIT prompt skills are generally portable; optional cache/browser helpers add Bash/jq/curl/hash utilities or MCP/package requirements.
risks: Manifest version ranges are not resolved installed versions, and latest documentation may not match a supported project release.
Mandatory ambiguity questions, cross-model offers and repeated per-invocation confirmation can conflict with autonomous authorized work.
Browser setup uses an unpinned latest package; accessibility-tree inspection cannot establish screen-reader acceptance.
Fetch cache keys query-shaped output by URL alone; the hit exposes the original prompt but blocks the new fetch, leaving suitability to later agent judgment.
Post-fetch HEAD obtains validators separately from the cached response, permitting content/validator mismatches.
Upstream evaluation scores and selected-skill traces do not prove success for this harness.
application: Keep one task router and add conditional craft references where they change decisions.
Ground version-sensitive work in resolved versions and suitable official sources.
Evaluate routing, runtime activation and finished artifacts as distinct stages.
If caching is justified, associate raw bytes with validators from the same response and include extraction query/version and relevant request variation.
Retain failed evaluation attempts and compare improvements on the same representative tasks.
